extracted.intended_audience: MathML implementers, renderer authors, and MathML content authors (browser developers, accessibility/rendering tool developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Specification-level rules and attributes for rendering MathML presentation elements (especially <mo>, linebreaking/indentation, spacing, stretching, mtext, mspace, ms, and grouping). Intended to guide implementers and authors on expected semantics and defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: rspace (trailing space)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies the trailing space appearing after the operator; set by dictionary (default: thickmathspace). Note that after is on the left in a RTL context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 3.2.5.6.4 Spacing around an operator. rspace should be interpreted as trailing/leading appropriately in RTL contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: stretchy attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean (set by dictionary; default false) specifying whether the operator should stretch to the size of adjacent material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When stretchy=true, characters obey the stretching rules (see 3.2.5.7). Renderers may only be able to stretch a subset of characters and may provide a discrete set of sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: symmetric attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean (set by dictionary; default false) that specifies whether the operator should be kept symmetric around the math axis when stretchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applies to vertically stretched symbols. If symmetric=true, height and depth above/below axis are forced equal by taking the maximum of the two (see vertical stretching algorithm).

rubrics_metrics.name: maxsize attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Length (set by dictionary; default unbounded) specifying the maximum size of the operator when stretchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unitless or percentage values indicate a multiple of the reference (unstretched) size. MathML 4 deprecates "infinity" since omitting the attribute is equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: minsize attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Length (set by dictionary; default 100%) specifying the minimum size of the operator when stretchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unitless or percentage values indicate a multiple of the reference (unstretched) size.

rubrics_metrics.name: largeop attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean (set by dictionary; default false) specifying whether the operator is considered a 'large' operator (drawn larger when displaystyle=true).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include integral and product characters (U+222B, U+220F). See 3.1.6 Displaystyle and Scriptlevel for more discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: movablelimits attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean (set by dictionary; default false) specifying whether under- and overscripts attached to this operator move to the compact sub-/superscript positions when displaystyle is false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical examples with movablelimits=true: sum, prod, and lim. See 3.1.6 for discussion of displaystyle/scriptlevel effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: accent attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean (set by dictionary; default false) specifying whether this operator should be treated as an accent when used as an underscript or overscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For compatibility with MathML Core, use accent=true on the enclosing mover and munderover instead of this attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: linebreak attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Controls desirability of a linebreak at this operator. Values: "auto" | "newline" | "nobreak" | "goodbreak" | "badbreak" (default: auto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "auto" uses the renderer's algorithm; "newline" forces a break; "nobreak" forbids a break; "goodbreak"/"badbreak" suggest good/poor positions. Comparisons are ASCII case-insensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: lineleading attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Length (inherited; default 100%) specifying the amount of vertical space to use after a linebreak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For tall lines, more leading may be clearer. Rendering agents may choose an appropriate default.

rubrics_metrics.name: linebreakstyle attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies whether a linebreak occurs 'before' or 'after' the operator, or whether the operator is duplicated. Values: "before" | "after" | "duplicate" | "infixlinebreakstyle" (set by dictionary; default before).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "before" places operator at beginning of new line (possibly indented); "after" places it at end of line before break; "duplicate" places it in both positions. "infixlinebreakstyle" uses the style specified for infix operators (application- or mstyle-bound).

rubrics_metrics.name: linebreakmultchar attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: String (inherited; default ⁢) specifying the character used to make an InvisibleTimes operator visible at a linebreak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: linebreakmultchar="·" would make the multiplication visible as a center dot at a break.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction of adjacent linebreak values
rubrics_metrics.description: linebreak values on adjacent mo and mspace elements do not interact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: linebreak=nobreak on an mo does not by itself inhibit a break on a preceding or following (possibly nested) mo or mspace element; it prevents breaks from occurring on either side of the mo in other situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: indentalign attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies positioning of lines when linebreaking takes place within an mrow. Values: "left" | "center" | "right" | "auto" | "id" (inherited; default auto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "auto" uses renderer's default indenting style. Renderers may ignore values if they would produce unusable lines given available width or font.

rubrics_metrics.name: indentshift attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Length (inherited; default 0) specifying an additional indentation offset relative to indentalign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentage values are relative to renderer's available horizontal space (current target width). Unitless numbers were allowed in MathML 3 but are deprecated in MathML 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: indenttarget attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: idref (inherited; default none) specifying the id of another element whose horizontal position determines the position of indented lines when indentalign=id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The referenced element must appear before being referenced. If id is unavailable or unsuitable, indentalign should revert to auto. Allows inter-expression alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: indentalignfirst attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies indentation style to use for the first line of a formula. Values: "left" | "center" | "right" | "auto" | "id" | "indentalign" (inherited; default indentalign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value 'indentalign' means to use the general indentalign value for the first line.

rubrics_metrics.name: indentshiftfirst attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Length or the keyword "indentshift" (inherited; default indentshift) specifying the offset to use for the first line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The keyword 'indentshift' means to use the same offset as the general indentshift. ASCII case-insensitive; percent and unitless numbers interpreted as for indentshift.

rubrics_metrics.name: indentalignlast attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies indentation style to use for the last line when a linebreak occurs. Values: "left" | "center" | "right" | "auto" | "id" | "indentalign" (inherited; default indentalign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When there are exactly two lines, this value should be used for the second line in preference to indentalign.

rubrics_metrics.name: indentshiftlast attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Length or the keyword "indentshift" (inherited; default indentshift) specifying the offset to use for the last line when a linebreak occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When there are exactly two lines, this value should be used for the second line in preference to indentshift. Percent/unitless interpretation same as indentshift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of indentalign values
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines semantics of indentalign options:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: left: align left side of next line to left of wrapping width; center: align center to center of wrapping width; right: align right side to right of wrapping width; auto: renderer's default (may vary with depth); id: align to left side of referenced element idref (revert to auto if not found).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator dictionary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Renderers are expected to have an operator dictionary of default attributes for mo elements indexed by content and form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an mo element is not listed, renderers should use the default values shown in the mo attributes table. Operator dictionary handles overloaded operators with different defaults per form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default heuristics for form attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: If form is not specified, renderer should infer prefix/infix/postfix according to context: first argument in mrow with more than one argument → prefix; last argument → postfix; only element in mrow in script position from 3.4 → postfix; otherwise infix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opening fences should have form="prefix" and closing fences form="postfix". If operator not in dictionary with specified form, renderer should choose available forms in preference order infix, postfix, prefix; if none available, use attribute defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for embellished operators
rubrics_metrics.description: An embellished operator (operator with nested scripts, surrounding text/whitespace, style changes, etc.) is treated as a whole for determining its form, but its surrounding spacing attributes are taken from the core mo element (or its dictionary entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise definition enumerates which elements count as embellished (mo or specific constructs like msub/msup/munder/mover/mrow containing one embellished operator plus space-like elements). This avoids most authors needing to specify form explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: lspace and rspace (spacing around an operator)
rubrics_metrics.description: lspace and rspace directly specify the horizontal space added around an operator (leading and trailing; interpreted appropriately in RTL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By convention, operators that bind tightly have smaller spacing than those that bind less tightly; operator dictionary should follow this. Non-graphical renderers should map spacing analogously (e.g., longer pauses). Some renderers may omit spacing inside subscripts/superscripts as TeX does.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stretching attributes overview
rubrics_metrics.description: stretchy, symmetric, maxsize and minsize govern whether/how an operator stretches to match other elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no attribute for specifying stretch direction; renderers decide which directions are reasonable. minsize/maxsize limit stretching (as multipliers or absolute units).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of minsize/maxsize values
rubrics_metrics.description: minsize and maxsize are multipliers of the operator's normal size or absolute sizes with units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: maxsize="300%" allows up to three times the unstretched size. minsize/maxsize are not used in the initial calculation of maximum heights/depths but constrain final sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of symmetric attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: If symmetric=true, computed height and depth are forced to be symmetric about the math axis by using the maximum of height-axis and depth+axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when parentheses should be symmetric; symmetric only applies to characters that stretch vertically (otherwise ignored).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embellished stretchy operator stretching
rubrics_metrics.description: If a stretchy mo element is embellished, the mo element at its core is stretched to a size based on the context of the embellished operator as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes embelished pairs (e.g., underlined/overlined parentheses) stretch to the same size they would without embellishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical stretching rules and when to stretch
rubrics_metrics.description: If a stretchy operator is a direct sub-expression of an mrow (or sole direct sub-expression of an mtd in a table row), it should stretch to cover the height and depth of the non-stretchy direct sub-expressions in that mrow or row, subject to minsize/maxsize constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies also to embellished stretchy operators (applies to core). Rules apply to inferred mrow. Symmetric rules only apply if symmetric=true and rowalign is baseline or axis. Most vertical arrows and most opening/closing fences defined in dictionary to stretch by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical stretching algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithm to compute height and depth of vertically stretched characters using maxheight, maxdepth, and axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Let maxheight and maxdepth be maximums among non-stretchy siblings; if symmetric=true then:
height = max(maxheight-axis, maxdepth+axis) + axis
depth = max(maxheight-axis, maxdepth+axis) - axis
Otherwise: height = maxheight, depth = maxdepth. If total size < minsize or > maxsize, increase/decrease both height and depth proportionately to meet constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical stretching in table cells (rowspan handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a stretchy operator is in an mtd, rules assume each cell covers exactly one row (rowspan=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the operator's cell spans multiple rows, it should only stretch vertically to cover those table cells entirely within the set of rows that the operator's cell covers; ignore cells extending into rows not covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontal stretching rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If a stretchy operator (or embellished core) is a direct sub-expression of an munder/mover/munderover, or the sole direct sub-expression of an mtd in some column, it should stretch to cover the width of the other direct sub-expressions in the element/column, subject to minsize/maxsize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default: most horizontal arrows and some accents stretch horizontally. Table handling assumes columnspan=1; ignore columns not covered by the operator's cell.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules common to vertical and horizontal stretching
rubrics_metrics.description: If a stretchy operator is not required to stretch, it uses standard (unstretched) font size. If required to stretch but all other expressions are also stretchy, all that can stretch should grow to the maximum of their normal unstretched sizes, subject to minsize/maxsize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: in an mrow containing only vertically stretchy operators, each should stretch to the maximum of their normal unstretched sizes unless restricted by minsize/maxsize or font limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: mtext element purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: An mtext element represents arbitrary text that should be rendered as itself; intended to denote commentary text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text with a clearly defined notational role should use mi or mo instead. mtext can contain renderable whitespace (which should have analogous effects in non-graphical media). See 2.1.7 Collapsing Whitespace in Input for whitespace handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: mtext attributes and warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: mtext elements accept mathematics style attributes common to token elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of warnings about legal grouping of space-like elements (3.2.7) and about the use of such elements for tweaking (MathML-Notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: mspace element role
rubrics_metrics.description: mspace empty element represents a blank space of any desired size as set by its attributes; can also be used to make linebreaking suggestions to a visual renderer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults are chosen to typically have no effect; mspace is generally used with explicit attribute values. Warning about legal grouping of space-like elements and tweaking as in MathML-Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: mspace attributes (width/height/depth and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: mspace accepts width (length; default 0em), height (length; default 0ex), depth (length; default 0ex); also accepts mathematics style attributes and indentation attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mathvariant and mathcolor have no effect; mathsize only affects interpretation of units in sizing attributes. Linebreaking on mspace is deprecated in MathML4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of space-like elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies which MathML presentation elements are considered space-like (i.e., typically render as whitespace and don't affect mathematical meaning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Space-like elements include: an mtext element that is empty or consists only of Unicode spacing characters; mspace, maligngroup, malignmark; mstyle/mphantom/mpadded whose direct sub-expressions are space-like; semantics whose first argument exists and is space-like; maction whose selected sub-expression exists and is space-like; an mrow all of whose direct sub-expressions are space-like. Note: mphantom is not automatically space-like unless its content is space-like.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal grouping of space-like elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Space-like elements are counted as arguments in elements that require a specific number of arguments; inserting space-like elements can change argument counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should group space-like elements with a neighboring argument using an mrow when necessary. Example: <msup><mi>x</mi><malignmark edge="right"/></msup> is illegal (msup must have exactly 2 arguments); the correct form groups the base and the mark inside an mrow.

rubrics_metrics.name: ms element (string literal) purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The ms element represents string literals for expressions intended to be interpreted by computer algebra systems or programming languages; by default displayed with double quotes and no extra spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ms content is made of characters/mglyphs, not ASCII strings. Content should be rendered with visible escaping of certain characters (including quotes and preferably whitespace other than single spaces) so the viewer sees exact characters in the literal. ms trims and collapses whitespace per 2.1.7 Collapsing Whitespace in Input.

rubrics_metrics.name: ms element attributes (lquote/rquote)
rubrics_metrics.description: ms elements accept lquote and rquote attributes (strings) to specify opening and closing quotes (defaults: U+0022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These define what characters visually enclose the string literal (note: 'left'/'right' semantics differ in RTL contexts).
